Phlebotomists collect blood samples for testing, transfusion, donation, or research, check patient identities and sample labels, hand samples over, explain procedures to patients, and observe adverse reactions. description.text: Explore phlebotomists' collection of blood samples for testing, transfusion, donation, or research, patient identity and sample label checks and handovers, procedure explanations, and observation of adverse reactions, along with identity mismatches, sample label errors, infection prevention gaps, adverse reactions or handover errors, and qualification boundaries; view US 2025 wages and 2025—2035 separate occupational projections.

subject.name: Phlebotomists
subject.summary: Phlebotomists (O*NET 31-9097.00) collect blood samples for testing, transfusion, donation, or research, check patient identities and sample labels, hand samples over, explain procedures to patients, and observe adverse reactions. Working with patient identities, test or collection requests, sample labels, times, and handover records, they produce identity-to-sample matching records, incident reports, and traceable handovers. Invasive blood collection, infection prevention, and adverse reaction management must be performed by trained and authorized personnel under institutional procedures. Work settings, qualifications, and final responsibility must be checked against local and institutional rules.
